days.title: Northern Peaks and Gorges
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Sierra del Pinar
stops.detail: Undoubtedly, the main distinctive feature of this complex is the Sierra del Pinar, of high altitude and visual dominance over the others, which is why its two slopes are visible from any point in the natural park.

stops.name: Garganta del Bocaleones
stops.detail: Also noteworthy is the presence of spectacularly spectacular gorges or canyons opened between limestone materials, such as the Garganta del Bocaleones, with a vertical drop of up to four hundred meters.

stops.name: cueva de la Ermita
stops.detail: Here you will find the Ermita cave or Ermita de la Garganta, of great beauty due to its dimensions, its formations of stalactites and stalagmites, its chromatic variety and the exuberant vegetation developed in the shadow of the canyon.

days.title: Karst Depressions and Viewpoints
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: La Manga de Villaluenga
stops.detail: The depression known as "La Manga de Villaluenga" stands out as one of the most striking and admired spots in the natural park.

stops.name: sima de Villaluenga
stops.detail: At the bottom of it, some characteristic forms of karst modeling can be observed, such as small poljes and sinkholes that occupy the deepest areas, where the great Villaluenga chasm is located.

days.title: Caves and Labyrinths
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: cueva del Gato
stops.detail: Highlights include the Gato cave, through which an underground river, after traveling five kilometers from the Hundidero chasm, reappears pouring its waters into the Guadiaro river; the Pileta cave, which contains cave paintings and can be visited with restrictions and using oil lamps; and the Garganta Verde, a narrow and deep gorge that serves as the only drainage for the entire Sierra del Pinar.

stops.name: Cancha Bermeja
stops.detail: In it we find the characteristic ruiniform or torcal-type landscapes, the result of differential erosion in the limestone banks, carving labyrinthine and capricious forms of great plastic beauty, the best examples of which are found in the spot known as "Cancha Bermeja", in the public forest of Sierra Blanquilla and in the Peñón del Berrueco, a limestone islet that represents the southern extension of the Sierra de Líbar.
